shared_qualifications: C1: source alloy formulas are atomic percentages, whereas CRA element columns are wt%. For a complete ternary formula, wt%_i = 100*x_i*M_i / sum(x_j*M_j). Atomic weights from CIAAW Abridged Standard Atomic Weights 2024 (https://ciaaw.org/abridged-atomic-weights.htm): Al26.982, Co58.933, Ce140.12, Ni58.693, Y88.906, Fe55.845, Gd157.25. Only relevant elements enter each explicitly stated ternary; no omitted alloy component is filled from CRA.

C2: V(SCE)*1000=mV(SCE); scale the printed +/- value by1000, then form mean-minus/plus uncertainty endpoints for the CRA Min/Max comparison. The source does not define the statistical meaning of +/-; these are not assumed observed extrema or standard deviations.

Table 2 uses approximately10^-4 cm2 electrodes in N2-deaerated0.6 M NaCl at pH6. The method is a 25 C one-hour OCP exposure followed by0.1 mV/s polarization (PDF p.3). When Epit is unclear, the authors use current two orders above ipass without identifying affected results; this qualification is retained rather than excluding outcomes.

Pure-Al Table 2 Epit=-0.701+/-0.016 V conflicts with CRA774=-550 mV and endpoints[-606,-494]. Material/medium/procedure still identify the sole pure-Al counterpart; the link is discrepant, not repaired.

CRA777/778 have identical composition and blank heat/microstructure fields. The amorphous Table 2 reading and its complete mean/uncertainty pattern identify777. The fully crystalline source reading -0.674+/-0.055 V disagrees with778(-583,[-793,-373]mV);778 is candidate-only because the source550 C/24 h state cannot be independently established in its missing processing metadata. No one-to-one elimination is imposed.

Figure 8 heat treatments at100 C for1,10,100 and1000 h are distinct from as-spun and fully crystalline550 C/24 h conditions (PDF p.3). Their separate outcomes are not merged merely because composition or potential overlaps a CRA row.
